How severity tails drive excess layer costs & ILFs

Reading

Under a moderate tail (σ = 1.00) at a $350k limit, 29.7% of expected loss sits in the excess layer and 4.0% of claims pierce above—giving an ILF of 1.48×.

Illustrative only: synthetic lognormal severities (σ = 0.55 / 1.00 / 1.55, $100k mean) via closed-form L(x) & SplitMix64 Box–Muller in Rust/WASM—excludes client data, ALAE, and treaty terms.

Source ↗ Actuarial Review ↗

Severity Parameterization

Each tail scenario holds ground-up expected severity fixed at E[X] = $100,000 by setting μ = ln(100,000) − σ²/2, isolating how tail thickness alone shifts loss cost out of primary retention into excess layers.

Closed-Form Layer Loss

Limited expected value is evaluated directly via L(x) = E[X]·Φ(z − σ) + x·Φ(−z) where z = (ln x − μ)/σ, using Abramowitz & Stegun 26.2.17 (max CDF error < 7.5×10⁻⁸).

Deterministic Verification

Every slider or tail change cross-checks closed-form expectations against a 65,536-draw SplitMix64 Box–Muller simulation (fixed seed 2026) compiled with zero external Rust crates to wasm32-unknown-unknown.

Independent Lab & Research

What I build outside of client work

GitHub profile ↗

I like turning mathematical ideas into fast, inspectable software. Outside of P&C consulting, my independent projects span actuarial tooling, numerical computing, and quantitative finance self-study.

Actuarial Tooling

Open Reserving Kernels

Pure-Rust actuarial kernels grounded in CAS/ASTIN literature—chain-ladder, BF/Benktander/Cape Cod/Brosius/Munich CL, Mack standard errors, ODP bootstrap, Iman–Conover dependence, and parametric ILFs—reserving-kernels ↗.

Quant Self-Study

Portfolio & Risk Systems

Independent study in quantitative finance—portfolio optimization, tail-risk measures such as CVaR, and asset-liability modeling—approached with the same rigor as insurance capital and balance-sheet risk.

Statistics

Bayesian Modeling & Calibration

Bayesian forecasting with calibration scorecards and deterministic, reproducible numerical experiments—the same toolkit behind credibility weighting, reserve variability, and model validation.
